The ISV is basically pointless now, near ceasing to exist. Which officially marked the end of war, a political party who proposed to run the government of the new Valddera accepted the deal with the breakaway nation, coming to an agreement to let Democracy into the nation. As the new post war government of Valddera is now a Democratic socialist republi, with the new president rumored to be called Harun Arman. The leader of the political party that came to power in Valddera, now the unified government and country finally rest after war. Everyone mourns for the people who lost their lives, either in battle, or anywhere else.[/Spoiler]

[Spoiler=New decisions of the government]The new government of Valddera doesn't change anything about the current relations and encourages to form new alliances and relations with other nations. The Valdderan Government also reaches out to Daesunite government to negotiate a new alliance that broke under the old government, urging for peace. This applies the same for the newly unified neighbors, Tirakan, Valddera wishes to make strong alliances and trades.

The Valdderan Government also request to join or partnership with the THEP alliance, to stabilize and refine the nations even more. As Valddera already has strong ties with some of the THEP members.

Valddera also proposes to cede the two occupied isles near Tirakan to the Tirakani nation, claiming to stabilize and improve relations with Tirakan and recognize the sovereignty of the new Government.

Valdderan Government also wishes to rejoin back the OIC organization, apologizing for their actions and wanting to restore stability and peace with other nations.[/spoiler]

[Spoiler=Sports and infrastructure rebuilding]The Valdderan Government quickly begins reconstructing and refining new buildings from the war conflict, using the brutalist architecture to rebuild and quickly arrange new homes. As this style of architecture costs less and has capacity, other than that Valddera quickly begins to reconstruct buildings and refine stadiums for the upcoming Erene world cup being hosted in the country. With proposals to have other nations come and help rebuild and refine buildings, stadiums and what's needed for living and infrastructure.[/spoiler]

[b]The Coalition, Part I[/b]

Minister Liukov, Chief Minister of Bolochia, stood up in his chair, addressing the House floor. It had been a contentious session in the House of Commons. The chamber was full of debate over a bill proposed by the Peoples Reform Party, the Public Land Default Act, which would re-codify a handful of laws, allowing the purchase of land on which debts had defaulted by any private body. The PRF argued that it was the right way to do things, and that allowing land to circulate back into the economy was a net positive.

[i]You understand the impact that this has. You know, sir, where the money for this bill is coming from.[/i] Liukov started, firm in his speech. [i]Or do I need to remind you, Representative Volkov, that KyraFuel made up the majority of your campaign funding?[/i]

Rhydian Volkov, PRF Rep from the Kyraniya District, stood in kind. [i]Is that your argument? That my election was financed? Is KyraPet in the room with us, sir?[/i]

[i]I dont think it unreasonable that KyraPet is trying the same, shady tricks as always. And I dont think it unreasonable that you would open the door for them to do so. We know who you are, there is no ignorance in this room.[/i]

Sam Kaaydell, a Conservation Party representative, joined Liukov in his condemnation, [i]The vagueness in phrasing here would open up any land, regardless of designation, for private purchase and use. Do you mean to tell us that this was intentional?

Yes, it was. It was a measure to open the flow of-[/i]

Kaaydell interrupted Volkov, [/i]So youd allow for protected lands, wildlife reserves, to fall right into the hands of the gas barons, with no way for protections to be enforced?

You all say this like its a sure thing, but its a competitive marke-

Theres a [b]history[/b], and our duty is to not repeat harmful histories. Surely you have much to gain, but you types always-

[b]Excuse you?[/b] Our types? Im Kyraniyan, same as you. We bear the same flag, Kaaydell.[/i] Volkov spat.

Kaaydell stood abruptly, [i]You never say that to me again. [b]We[/b], Volkov, are Koranvistanis. But that is where our similarities end![/i]

Volkov chuckled, [i]Oh, I forgot you were a-

You stop right there, sir![/i] Martin Zolyusk, KNP speaker from the Grigoriy-Shinov district, shouted over the growing commotion. [i]There is no justification for that behavior In-House.[/i]

And the unfriendly discussions continued long into the evening. Little progress was made. The same issue was put to vote 8 different times, before being tabled for other matters. Meeting transcripts were released 48 hours later, to some controversy.
